document_metadata.document_title: New Jersey Stormwater BMP Manual / N.J.A.C. 7:8 (city MS4 follows NJDEP standards)

design_criteria.water_quality_volume_method: NJDEP Water Quality Design Storm (WQDS): 1.25 inches of rain falling nonuniformly over 2 hours (N.J.A.C. 7:8-5.5). NRCS methodology computes WQDS runoff volume, peak rate, and hydrograph; BMPs such as small-scale bioretention must store/treat the entire WQDS volume.
peak_flow_calculation_method: USDA NRCS methodology (NRCS Runoff Equation and Dimensionless Unit Hydrograph)

evidence.excerpt: City of Newark MS4 follows NJDEP Stormwater BMP Manual
WQDS: 1.25 inches of rain falling nonuniformly over 2 hours
The capacity of the underdrain must be sufficient to allow the system to drain within 72 hours
evidence.page_or_section: Green Infrastructure BMPs, Chapter 9.7: Small-Scale Bioretention Systems (Page 74 / c0092)

evidence.excerpt: If the small-scale bioretention system with underdrain is installed in an area subject to pedestrian traffic, the drain time should be reduced to 24 hours
The 72 hour maximum has not been exceeded, meaning the procedure may be continued
the minimum depth of 18 inches may not be sufficient
In sloped-bottom systems, the maximum longitudinal slope is 10%
The seasonal high water table (SHWT) must be at least 1 foot below the bottom of the gravel layer
which is greater than the 2 ft mimimum separation requirement
For the WQDS, the maximum depth of runoff is 18 inches at the down-gradient end of a sloped-bottom system
The depth of runoff above the surface of the soil bed is 12 in
Small-scale bioretention systems are stormwater management
Note that an MTD is used for pretreatment so that exfiltration may be used

extraction_quality.review_notes: No durable Newark city design-manual PDF; municipality record via NJDEP BMP Manual (removed prior newark→NJDEP alias that caused state_only).

design_parameters.enrich_notes: WQDS rainfall depth (1.25 in per N.J.A.C. 7:8-5.5) is not stated in these excerpts. SHWT separation is explicitly 1 ft below gravel (underdrain bioretention) and 2 ft minimum between basin/soil bed bottom and SHWT (infiltration example)—not collapsed to one value. Ponding/runoff depth above soil bed is capped at 12 in (planter/underdrain example) and 18 in max at down-gradient for sloped-bottom bioretention swale under WQDS. Design exfiltration commonly uses half of tested saturated hydraulic conductivity (site-specific). Pedestrian areas: underdrain bioretention drain time reduced to 24 hr vs 72 hr general maximum.
